name: ChurchPay
shortDescription: A UK church platform combining public websites, member records, giving and Gift Aid, services, pastoral care, communications and treasurer reporting.
suitableContexts: UK churches seeking a payment, Gift Aid and people-administration platform
Church groups and networks needing separate church identities and cross-church reporting

pricing.summary: ChurchPay publishes Essentials from £149/month annually or £169 monthly for one church, Complete from £229/month annually or £259 monthly, and Group from £349/month for two churches plus £119 per additional church. The supplier states no giving transaction markup is charged by its subscription.

startingPrice.qualifier: Essentials, billed annually, for a single church

tiers.label: Essentials
tiers.detail: Single church; website, member portal, giving and Gift Aid scope

tiers.label: Complete
tiers.detail: Adds pastoral care, newcomer pipeline and reporting

tiers.label: Group
tiers.detail: Two churches; £119 per additional church is stated

gdprInformation: ChurchPay publishes a privacy policy identifying the church as usual controller and Neural Network Group Limited as processor for hosted records. It describes roles, data categories and possible international transfers. Ask the supplier for its current data-processing agreement and detailed sub-processor list.
importExport: Supplier describes HMRC-ready exports for Gift Aid and GASDS

uk-purchasing.value: Supplier pricing is published in GBP and its privacy policy identifies an England-registered operating company.

gbp-pricing.value: Published subscriptions begin at £149/month on annual billing for one church.

gift-aid.value: Supplier describes Gift Aid and GASDS records and HMRC-ready exports.

data-processing.value: Published privacy material describes controller and processor roles and possible international-transfer safeguards.

editorial.assessment: ChurchPay is a higher-priced UK all-in-one option that puts giving, reconciliation and Gift Aid alongside public website and people administration. Its value depends on whether the church genuinely needs that joined-up payment-first model; the finance lead, pastoral lead and website owner should each test their workflow rather than assuming a single platform will reduce all administration.
bestFor: UK churches wanting giving, Gift Aid and treasurer reporting with a shared people record
Groups or networks needing separate church identities and cross-church reporting
Teams that value a supplier walkthrough before evaluating a full platform
strengths: Public GBP plans identify single-church and group scope
Giving, Gift Aid, public website, pastoral care and reporting are explicitly part of the product
The supplier publishes UK privacy and controller/processor information
limitations: Ask for the current trial route, data-processing agreement, sub-processor list, hosting location, export formats and accessibility information
Base subscription pricing is materially higher than several directory alternatives
Gift Aid, money handling and pastoral notes still require church-led controls and review

procurementVerdict.differentiator: Giving and treasurer reporting are presented as central alongside church administration
